title: Rank immutable evidence over mutable status in three-way merge
context: Merges silently reverted bug closures. The tiebreak in pickWinner used status fields (which move bidirectionally, e.g., fixed→open on reopen), so a record with fixed_commit:null and status:open would lexicographically win over one with fixed_commit:sha and status:fixed, losing the closure deterministically without reporting conflict. Touches invariant(s): con_902759b3dc (All JSON writes to .hunch/ must be atomic (temp-file + rename) so an interrupted write can never truncate the index); con_a87360128b (Semantic vectors are a derived layer in SQLite, never the source of truth; reconcile by content hash on reindex).
decision: Insert a resolution tier before the lexicographic tiebreak that ranks one-way lifecycle evidence (fixed_commit, spawned_decision/constraint, superseded_by, valid_to) — immutable historical facts — instead of status strings. Evidence is authoritative because it records what happened; status is mutable and can move in both directions.
consequences: Closures no longer revert silently on merge
Genuine reopens (human-confirmed status changes) still win over older evidence via the earlier human-confirmation tier
Merge is now explicit about distinguishing history from state
Prevents non-deterministic loss in the one subsystem whose job is not losing state
alternatives_rejected: Status-first tiebreak (original behavior) — silently drops closures
Deterministic content tiebreak alone — no way to encode semantic intent
Letting merge conflicts surface — defeats structured merge purpose
